thread: The price of your inputs and the shape of your plumbing moved in opposite directions. OpenAI's record $122B round at $852B post and Anthropic's $965B valuation set the pricing umbrella over API pricing and talent costs — inputs you do not control. The 2026-07-28 MCP spec hands back one you do: stateless request/response scales horizontally behind an ordinary load balancer, at the price of broken cross-version compatibility and four deprecations on a 12-month runway. Spend the effort where the lever is — your servers, not your vendor's price list.

items.headline: MCP's 2026-07-28 spec moves the core from stateful to stateless request/response
items.why: Your MCP servers become ordinary stateless web services — horizontal scale behind a plain load balancer, no sticky sessions, no shared session store. The cost is a hard migration: cross-version compatibility breaks, and Roots, Sampling, Logging, and Dynamic Client Registration are all deprecated on a 12-month clock, so anything you built on those needs a replacement designed now.
items.example: Because compatibility breaks across versions, a client pinned to the old spec cannot talk to a new server — so you run both fleets during the cutover rather than upgrading in place.
items.connection: Read with the mega-rounds item: you don't set the price of your inputs, but the cost of running your own servers is one you still control.

items.headline: OpenAI closes record $122B round ($852B post); Anthropic at $965B
items.why: Anthropic raised $965B, and OpenAI closed a record $122B round at an $852B post-money valuation. Frontier-lab rounds at approximately $1T valuations set the pricing umbrella you build under — they move both API pricing and what you pay for talent.
items.connection: Read with the MCP spec change: the pricing umbrella is set above you, so the engineering cost you can still cut is in your own servers.
